patients.label: 35-year-old man with acute carbon monoxide poisoning who developed acute pulmonary edema during hyperbaric oxygen therapy
attribution_limitations: The case text reports sinus tachycardia on the only 12-lead ECG, while the discussion says the electrocardiographic assessment revealed normal findings. Both refer to the same test, but the discussion is an interpretive summary and states no rhythm or value that contradicts the case text, so this is kept as an ambiguity rather than a source conflict.

The abstract says emergency chest CT showed APE, while the case text describes an initial CT without notable pulmonary abnormalities and a later follow-up pulmonary CT; the source does not say which CT the abstract means.

The names diuretics, corticosteroids and bronchodilators are given in one sentence and furosemide, methylprednisolone and diprophylline in another; the source does not state which drug belongs to which class, and the route intravenous precedes only furosemide.
The Figure 3 caption dates the repeat CT 5 days after treatment without saying which treatment; the text places it after endotracheal tube removal at 48 hours.

The discussion links the mediastinal and subcutaneous emphysema and pneumothorax mechanistically to severe coughing and attributes pulmonary edema to noncardiac mechanisms; these are authors' interpretations.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1.
CT performed at the time of admission demonstrated hypodense lesions within the bilateral globus pallidus. CT = computed tomography.

Figure 2.
CT performed after HBOT demonstrated bilateral pulmonary exudative changes, subcutaneous emphysema, pneumomediastinum, and pneumothorax. CT = computed tomography, HBOT = hyperbaric oxygen therapy.

Figure 3.
A repeat CT performed 5 days after treatment demonstrated significant improvement in pulmonary edema with complete resolution of the subcutaneous, mediastinal, and subpleural gases. CT = computed tomography.
